chapter: Cap, the city and its dances
title: Tom's train trips for rehearsals and travel time to the coast
summary: Tom Albert came early by train for rehearsals with Julius's father; the trip took about two hours.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: No, you couldn't do that today. But, uh, they had, uh, this fellow Frank Toad, he used to be around by my daddy all the time. I used to come to my daddy's house and my daddy used to have rehearsal. That's why, uh, Punchfield's got to be so good. My dad used to call rehearsal twice a week. And, uh, well, they didn't, he didn't worry about Tom after rehearsing because, uh, when Tom would come over, my daddy would tell him, you know, what number they would rehearsal, this number, that number. And, uh, he'd sit around. He'd always lead that three or four hours, you know, before time. Because, uh, he'd come on the train. Well, they didn't have, uh, say, and time if the train would leave from here and go over to New Orleans. I mean, to the pass. If he'd wait for the next train, he'd be too late to get on the job with my daddy, you see.
How long did it take to get from New Orleans to the pass that way?

I think about two hours. Two hours, maybe two hours and a half. And that's not bad, really. No. Well, nah, I mean, the best they are now. It still takes almost an hour. Nah, you take... I see so many people make it from over here in a car, 45 minutes. And some make it an hour. And when I leave, if it's two hours, it's alright with me now because I don't be in all that big a hurry. Right. But some, so many of them now, you'll find they turn upside down on the highway. And since they build this high at 10, I'd rather go to the old highway than go to the high at 10 now because they go too fast. Now, did you know, oh yeah, you had this guy's name? Oh, I can't call his name. I can't call his name. Because there's so many guys that I played with here since I've been here. And so many of them has passed, you know.
